title: Mercury Hits 800 Degrees and Still Has Ice

scenes.text: Mercury hits 800 degrees, and it still has ice.
In the day, the surface gets hot enough to melt lead.
But near its poles, some craters never see a single ray of sunlight.
Inside them, NASA's MESSENGER spacecraft found water ice.
Some of it is bare on the surface. Some is hidden under a thin dark layer.
The hottest-looking planet next to the Sun is hiding ice.

description:
The surface of Mercury can reach 800 degrees Fahrenheit, yet NASA's MESSENGER found water ice in permanently shadowed craters near its poles.
Some ice is bare at the surface and some is under a thin dark layer.
Where else do you think ice could be hiding in the solar system?
first_comment: Bonus: the ice was spotted by radar from Earth first, then confirmed by spacecraft. Where would you send a probe next?
